stated.text: The rules engine is a Node.js module at src/chess.js.
src/chess.js is a CommonJS module (loadable with require).
The module has no dependencies.
npm test runs node --test.
A position is a FEN string.
startFen() returns the standard start position.
legalMoves(fen) returns an array of every legal move for the side to move.
legalMoves returns moves in UCI form (for example e2e4).
legalMoves writes a promotion in UCI form with the piece letter (for example e7e8q).
legalMoves returns its moves sorted alphabetically.
applyMove(fen, move) returns the FEN after the move.
The FEN applyMove returns has correct castling rights.
The FEN applyMove returns has the correct en-passant square.
The FEN applyMove returns has the correct halfmove clock.
The FEN applyMove returns has the correct fullmove number.
applyMove throws IllegalMoveError when the move is not legal.
IllegalMoveError is a class the module also exports.
The en-passant target square is set after every two-square pawn push, whether or not a capture is possible (the FEN-spec convention).
status(fen) returns ongoing, check, checkmate or stalemate for the side to move.
All piece moves are implemented (king, queen, rook, bishop, knight, pawn).
Castling is implemented on both sides (kingside and queenside).
Castling is never allowed out of check.
Castling is never allowed through check.
Castling is never allowed into check.
In UCI, castling is the king's two-square move: e1g1, e1c1, e8g8, e8c8.
En passant is implemented.
Promotion to q, r, b or n is implemented.
Check is implemented (a move that leaves the mover's own king in check is not legal, and status reports check).
Checkmate is implemented.
Stalemate is implemented.
There are node --test tests in test/ covering the known game fool's mate.
There are node --test tests in test/ covering the known game scholar's mate.
There are node --test tests in test/ covering castling.
There are node --test tests in test/ covering en passant.
There are node --test tests in test/ covering promotion.
There are node --test tests in test/ covering stalemate.
There are node --test tests in test/ covering move counts from standard test positions.
legalMoves on a middlegame position takes under 50 ms.
A depth-2 legal-move count of the start position takes under 2 seconds.
npm test passes.

unstated.text: What legalMoves, applyMove and status do when the FEN itself is malformed or impossible (empty string, wrong number of ranks or squares, unknown piece letter, bad side-to-move field, trailing whitespace or newline, a side with no king).
unstated.why: A caller passing a FEN typed by a person or read from a file needs a clear failure rather than a crash deep inside, a silently wrong move list, or an infinite loop; the maintainer needs to know which error type to expect.
unstated.probe: In node: const c = require('./src/chess.js'); for each of '', 'garbage', 'rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP w KQkq - 0 1' (7 ranks), 'rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR x KQkq - 0 1', startFen() + '\n', '8/8/8/8/8/8/8/8 w - - 0 1' call c.legalMoves(f), c.status(f) and c.applyMove(f, 'e2e4') inside try/catch and print the result or the error's constructor name and message.
unstated.fine_answers: Throwing a descriptive Error (a plain Error, a distinct invalid-FEN error class, or IllegalMoveError) is fine; tolerating surrounding whitespace is fine; what is not fine is returning a confident but wrong answer or hanging. Which one is chosen should be consistent across the three functions.

unstated.text: Whether a FEN without the halfmove and fullmove fields (the four-field form common in EPD test suites and many tools) is accepted.
unstated.why: Standard test positions are often published without the two counters; a user pasting one would expect it to work or to get a clear message.
unstated.probe: Call legalMoves('rnbqkbnr/pppppppp/8/8/8/8/PPPPPPPP/RNBQKBNR w KQkq -') and applyMove on the same string with 'e2e4'; print the results or the error.
unstated.fine_answers: Accept it with defaults 0 and 1 (and output the full six fields), or reject it with a clear error.

unstated.text: How applyMove treats move strings that are not well-formed UCI or that differ only in form from a legal move: uppercase ('E2E4', 'e7e8Q'), surrounding spaces, a promotion with no piece letter ('e7e8'), a promotion letter on a non-promoting move ('e2e4q'), off-board squares ('e2e9'), a non-string, and king-takes-rook castling ('e1h1').
unstated.why: A caller relaying user input needs to know whether these throw IllegalMoveError, some other error, or are silently accepted; auto-queening a bare 'e7e8' or accepting 'e2e4q' would change the game without the caller knowing.
unstated.probe: On startFen() call applyMove with 'E2E4', ' e2e4', 'e2e4q', 'e2e9', 42 and print result or error class; on '4k3/4P3/8/8/8/8/8/4K3 w - - 0 1' call applyMove with 'e7e8' and 'e7e8Q'; on 'r3k2r/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K2R w KQkq - 0 1' call applyMove with 'e1h1'.
unstated.fine_answers: Rejecting everything that is not exactly in legalMoves(fen) with IllegalMoveError is fine; accepting case-insensitive input is fine if documented; auto-queening a bare promotion is acceptable only if documented.

unstated.text: What the exported IllegalMoveError looks like to a caller: whether it extends Error, its name, and whether its message names the rejected move.
unstated.why: Callers will write catch blocks with instanceof IllegalMoveError or instanceof Error and log the message; a class that does not extend Error loses the stack trace and breaks generic error handling.
unstated.probe: try { c.applyMove(c.startFen(), 'e2e5') } catch (e) { console.log(e instanceof c.IllegalMoveError, e instanceof Error, e.name, e.message, !!e.stack) }
unstated.fine_answers: Extending Error with name 'IllegalMoveError' and a message that includes the move (and optionally the FEN) is the expected shape; exact message wording is free.

unstated.text: Whether the input FEN's castling rights are trusted when they disagree with the board (a right listed but the king or that rook is not on its home square).
unstated.why: With an inconsistent FEN, a generator that trusts the field can offer a castle that moves a missing rook or produce a corrupted board, giving wrong move lists and wrong counts.
unstated.probe: Call legalMoves('4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K3 w K - 0 1') and legalMoves('4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/R3K3 w KQ - 0 1') and check whether e1g1 is listed; if so, applyMove with 'e1g1' and print the FEN.
unstated.fine_answers: Not offering the castle when the king or rook is missing, or rejecting the FEN as invalid, are both fine.

unstated.text: How draws other than stalemate are handled: the fifty-move rule (halfmove clock at 100 or more), insufficient material (for example king against king), and repetition (which a FEN alone cannot see).
unstated.why: status only has ongoing, check, checkmate and stalemate; a user building a game on this module would want to know whether status reports K v K as ongoing and whether legalMoves keeps generating moves past the fifty-move limit, and a caller switching on the four values would break if a new value such as 'draw' appeared.
unstated.probe: Call status and legalMoves on '4k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K3 w - - 0 1' and on 'r3k3/8/8/8/8/8/8/4K2R w - - 100 80'; print the results.
unstated.fine_answers: Keeping status to the four stated values and reporting these as ongoing (or check) while documenting that other draws are out of scope is fine; adding a separate draw helper is fine; adding a fifth status value is a change the customer should be asked about.

unstated.text: Which standard test positions and depths the move-count tests check, and so how far move generation is actually verified beyond depth 2 (pins, discovered check by en passant, castling-right loss when a rook is captured, promotion captures).
unstated.why: Subtle move-generation bugs usually show only at depth 3 or more or in positions like Kiwipete; the customer and the next maintainer rely on these counts as the proof the engine is correct.
unstated.probe: With a small perft helper built on legalMoves and applyMove, count start position depth 3 (expect 8902) and depth 4 (197281), Kiwipete 'r3k2r/p1ppqpb1/bn2pnp1/3PN3/1p2P3/2N2Q1p/PPPBBPPP/R3K2R w KQkq - 0 1' depth 1 (48), 2 (2039), 3 (97862), and position 3 '8/2p5/3p4/KP5r/1R3p1k/8/4P1P1/8 w - - 0 1' depth 4 (43238); also list which positions and depths the test files in test/ check.
unstated.fine_answers: Any set of published perft positions is fine as long as the counts match the published values; depth 3 or 4 on the start position plus Kiwipete is a common minimum.

unstated.text: How the two speed limits are measured: which middlegame position the 50 ms budget refers to, whether it is the first (cold) call or a warm one, on what machine, and whether npm test checks the limits at all.
unstated.why: Without a named position and a test, the limits can be missed silently or a slow CI machine can fail the suite intermittently; the next maintainer needs to know what number is guarded.
unstated.probe: Time legalMoves on the Kiwipete FEN once cold and averaged over 100 calls, and time the depth-2 count of startFen() (expect 400); then search test/ for timing assertions and note the position and threshold they use.
unstated.fine_answers: A test that asserts the limits with some headroom on a named position is fine; measuring warm or cold is fine if stated; leaving speed out of npm test is acceptable if the measured numbers are reported.

unstated.text: Whether there is any written description of the module's API, its error behaviour and how to run the tests (a README or doc comments).
unstated.why: The next person using or maintaining the module needs the function signatures, the UCI and FEN conventions (including the always-set en-passant square) and the error contract without reading the source.
unstated.probe: List the files in the delivered repository and read any README or the top of src/chess.js for a description of startFen, legalMoves, applyMove, status and IllegalMoveError.
unstated.fine_answers: A short README, JSDoc comments in src/chess.js, or both are fine.
